transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Lindqvist, thank you for meeting with me. I wanted to sit down and talk to you about your CT scan and your care over the last day.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I've been waiting. I know the results came back yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. So, there was some of a situation with how the imaging was handled. There was some confusion with the report.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? I'm a former paramedic. Don't give me the runaround. Was there a PE on the scan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, it turns out that there was an issue. The preliminary report didn't mention the pulmonary embolism, and the results weren't read by the attending radiologist until later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you had a clot in my lung and you just left it there for eighteen hours.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion this caused, but we were really busy in the radiology department yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Busy is not a reason to miss a PE on a CT. That is a critical failure.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I know this is frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating is an understatement. I was lying here while a clot was potentially moving.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, I have to get back to the floor soon, but I want to make sure we fix this now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're rushing me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm just saying we need to move forward with the treatment plan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to know exactly why it wasn't seen.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, there were some things that didn't go quite right with the reporting sequence.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You still haven't told me if the error was the radiologist or if the Resident on call ignored the image.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a breakdown in the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Whatever. Just tell me what happens now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Okay, so here is the exact plan. First, we have already started you on a Heparin drip. I have the nurse coming in within the next ten minutes to calibrate the pump and check your baseline PTT.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Once the PTT is stable, which should be in about four hours, we will transition you to a subcutaneous Enoxaparin injection twice daily. You will be the one to alert the nurse if you feel any sudden shortness of breath or chest pain during the transition.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I know how the protocol works.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll also be ordering a follow-up chest CT in seventy-two hours to ensure the clot is resolving. I will personally review that report as soon as it hits the system and I'll come back to this room to discuss it with you by 10:00 AM that day.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the error?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have already filed a formal incident report through the hospital's safety system. The department head for radiology is reviewing the timestamp of the scan versus the report to implement a new double-check system for all emergency CTs so this doesn't happen to another patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It doesn't change the eighteen hours I lost.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. But we have the medication running now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I guess.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be back in an hour to check your vitals. If you have any questions before then, use the call button and ask for me specifically.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language ('I have to get back to the floor soon', 'we need to move forward') which the patient explicitly calls out.

E.justification: The error is named (missed PE), but there are no comprehension checks performed throughout the conversation.

A.justification: A direct apology is offered, but it is immediately diluted by an excuse ('but we were really busy in the radiology department').

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand', 'I know this is frustrating') without naming specific emotions or engaging deeply with the patient's distress.

T.justification: Resident provides specific steps (Heparin, Enoxaparin, follow-up CT) with timelines, defines the patient's role in monitoring symptoms, and addresses systemic prevention via the incident report.
